newsitem.title: UKRAINE: CHERNOBYL CLOSURE HINGES ON EBRD DECISION-OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: CHERNOBYL CLOSURE HINGES ON EBRD DECISION-OFFICIAL.

text.p: Ukraine may not be able to close its Chernobyl reactor by 2000 if the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development does not provide the funding for two new nuclear reactors, a bank director said on Wednesday.

Ukraine, which has promised the Group of Seven (G-7) industrialised nations to shut the site of the world's worst nuclear accident, is waiting for the EBRD to decide whether it will finance the reactors that will replace power lost by Chernobyl's closure.
"I am expecting the decision will be positive," Yuri Poluneev told a news conference. "But if it isn't it will throw Ukraine's memorandum with the G-7 into question."

Poluneev, appointed to his post by the Ukrainian government, said EBRD leaders must decide whether the $1.2 billion construction of the reactors at Khmelnytsky and Rivne in western Ukraine were the least costly option to meet the bank's funding requirements.
Nuclear experts evaluating the project disagree on the cost of the proposed project.

Yuri Kostenko, Ukraine's top Chernobyl negotiator, said this week he expected the EBRD and G-7 to decide in Ukraine's favour but said the bank's failure to support the project could delay the planned closure date.

Ukraine's memorandum with the G-7 to close Chernobyl in exchange for $3.1 billion was signed last year just before the 10th anniversary of the April 26 1986 disaster which sent a radiation cloud over neighbouring Russia, Belarus and Europe.
Chernobyl will be on the G-7's agenda at its Denver summit next month when it considers a $780 million project to stabilise the concrete "sarcophagus" enclosing the ruined fourth reactor. REUTER
